content: The magnitude of the leprosy problem among women in a specific area—whether global, national, state, province, district, village, urban area, or health center—provides insight into the accessibility of leprosy services for women. It also indirectly reflects the quality of services provided. The proportion of foreign-born cases among new leprosy cases refers to the percentage of foreign-born individuals diagnosed with leprosy and registered for multidrug therapy (MDT) out of the total new cases detected during the reporting year. This information is derived from patient records available at various administrative levels (national, state, province, district). To calculate this proportion, all new foreign-born leprosy cases registered for MDT during the year are enumerated, divided by the total new cases detected in the area, and multiplied by 100. This proportion, reported annually as a percentage, indicates the extent of local leprosy transmission in a given area and reflects the accessibility and quality of leprosy services for foreign-born individuals. The number of relapses in a year refers to the total number of leprosy cases diagnosed as relapses and reported as such during the reporting year in a specific area. This data is obtained from patient records at various administrative levels. To calculate this, all diagnosed relapse cases during the year are enumerated and reported as absolute numbers. This indicator reflects the quality of treatment services provided and the magnitude of leprosy transmission. A rising number of relapses may suggest the circulation of drug-resistant strains. The treatment completion or cure rate of multibacillary (MB) cases is the proportion of MB cases that completed MDT within 18 months from the start of treatment among those registered for MDT in a given year. This is calculated through cohort analysis, where a cohort consists of patients who started MDT in a specific year. For example, all MB cases registered for MDT two years prior to the reporting year (Y-2 cohort) are analyzed. From this cohort, the number of MB cases completing treatment within 18 months is counted and multiplied by 100 to obtain the percentage. This rate, reported annually, indicates the proportion of patients completing treatment on time and reflects the quality of services provided, supervision, and patient care in a specific area. The treatment completion or cure rate of paucibacillary (PB) cases is the proportion of PB cases that completed MDT within 9 months from the start of treatment among those registered for MDT in a given year. Similar to MB cases, this is calculated through cohort analysis. For PB cases, the cohort consists of patients registered for MDT one year prior to the reporting year (Y-1 cohort). The number of PB cases completing treatment within 9 months is counted and multiplied by 100 to obtain the percentage. This rate, reported annually, reflects the quality of services provided, supervision, and patient care in a specific area. The percentage of household contacts screened among registered household contacts refers to the proportion of household contacts of registered leprosy patients who were screened for leprosy during the year. This data is derived from patient records at health facilities. To calculate this, the number of household contacts screened during the year is divided by the total number of registered household contacts in the area and multiplied by 100. This percentage, reported annually, indicates the coverage of case detection among household contacts, who are at the highest risk of contracting leprosy. A higher percentage is desirable as it reflects better screening and prevention efforts. The Global Leprosy Strategy 2016–2020: Accelerating Towards a Leprosy-Free World was officially launched on April 20, 2016. Its overarching goal is to further reduce the burden of leprosy while ensuring comprehensive and timely care based on principles of equity and social justice. The strategy is structured around three strategic pillars: strengthening government ownership and partnerships, stopping leprosy and its complications, and ending discrimination while promoting inclusion. The Operational Manual accompanying this strategy provides guidance for national leprosy program managers to adapt and implement the strategy in their respective countries. It includes suggested actions under each strategic pillar, which can be tailored to national contexts to achieve the global targets set for 2020. The manual was developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) with input from key stakeholders, including national program managers, technical agencies, funding agencies, and nongovernmental organizations.
